passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of Sysco’s financial condition, results of operations and liquidity and capital resources for the fiscal years ended June 27, 2026 and June 28, 2025 should be read as a supplement to our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes contained in Item 8 of this report, and in conjunction with the “Forward-looking Statements” section set forth in Part II and the “Risk Factors” section set forth in Item 1A of Part I. All discussion of changes in our results of operations from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2024 has been omitted from this Form 10-K, but may be found in Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Form 10-K for the year ended June 28, 2025, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on August 22, 2025. Overview Sysco distributes food and related products to restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments and other foodservice customers. Our primary operations are in North America and Europe. Under the accounting provisions related to disclosures about segments of an enterprise, we have combined certain operations into three reportable segments. “Other” financial information is attributable to our other operations that do not meet the quantitative disclosure thresholds. • U.S. Foodservice Operations – primarily includes (a) our U.S. Broadline operations, which distribute a full line of food products, including custom-cut meat, seafood, produce, specialty Italian, specialty imports and a wide variety of non-food products and (b) our U.S. Specialty operations, which include our FreshPoint fresh produce 32 distribution business, our Buckhead | Newport Meat & Seafood specialty protein operations, our growing Italian Specialty platform anchored by Greco & Sons, Inc., our Edward Don restaurant equipment and supplies distribution business, our Asian specialty distribution company and a number of other small specialty businesses that are not material to the operations of Sysco; • International Foodservice Operations – includes operations outside of the United States (U.S.), which distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products. The Americas primarily consists of operations in Canada, Bahamas, Costa Rica and Panama, as well as our export operations that distribute to international customers. Our European operations primarily consist of operations in the United Kingdom (U.K.), France, Ireland and Sweden; • SYGMA – our U.S. customized distribution operations serving quick-service chain restaurant customer locations; and • Other – primarily our hotel supply operations, Guest Worldwide. We estimate that we serve about 18% of an approximately $377 billion annual foodservice market in the U.S. based on industry data obtained from Technomic, Inc. (Technomic) as of the end of calendar year 2025. Technomic projects the market size to increase to approximately $390 billion by the end of calendar year 2026. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following discussion of “risk factors” identifies the most significant factors that may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial position and future financial performance. This information should be read in conjunction with Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations and the consolidated financial statements and related notes contained in this report. The following discussion of risks is not all inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are the most significant factors to consider when evaluating our business. These factors could cause our future results to differ from our expectations expressed in the forward-looking statements identified within “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and from other historical trends. Risk Factor Summary The following is a summary of the principal risks that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows, or the value of our securities. This summary does not describe all of the risks we face and should be read together with the more detailed discussion of the risk factors set forth below in this Item 1A and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently deem immaterial, may also impair our business. Industry and General Economic Risks • Our industry is characterized by low margins, and periods of significant or prolonged inflation or deflation affect our product costs and may negatively impact our profitability and results of operations. • A shortage of qualified labor and increases in labor costs could adversely affect our business and materially reduce earnings. • Global health developments and economic uncertainty resulting from global public health crises may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. • Unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, as well as unfavorable conditions in particular local markets, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. • We may not be able to fully compensate for increases in fuel costs, and fuel hedging arrangements intended to contain fuel costs could result in above market fuel costs, any of which could adversely affect our results of operations. • Economic and political instability and changes in laws and regulations could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. • Competition and the impact of GPOs may reduce our margins and make it difficult for us to maintain our market share, growth rate and profitability. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure and shareholder distributions combined, leaving residual internal liquidity after the dividend and buyback programme. This self-funding capacity underpins the investment-grade profile despite thin wholesale grocery margins and modest absolute profitability.

The current ratio sits above the sector median and improved year on year, reflecting adequate working capital to support daily foodservice distribution and short-dated inventory turns. Liquidity is further reinforced by an unrestricted cash balance that materially offsets gross borrowings on a net basis.

key_risks.text: The risk factors flag that the industry is characterized by low margins, with prolonged inflation or deflation affecting product costs and profitability. Our operating margin sits far below the sector median and softened year on year, so cost pass-through timing remains the central earnings sensitivity for this distributor.

Gross leverage is above the sector median and edged higher year on year, while net leverage also exceeds the peer median. The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, and headroom to the next leverage band boundary is thin, so a modest EBITDA decline or incremental borrowing could shift the assessment.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate in absolute terms but sits below the sector median and declined year on year, with EBITDA-based coverage similarly weaker than peers. Cash flow to debt also trails the sector median, indicating comparatively heavier reliance on a large debt stack relative to internally generated cash.

The maturity ladder is manageable, with the next twelve months representing only a modest slice of total borrowings and no single year presenting a concentrated refinancing wall. Free cash flow to debt improved year on year, supporting our judgement that scheduled amortisation and maturities can be met from internal resources.

overall_credit_view.text: We view the credit as sound but positioned below higher-rated distribution peers: leverage above sector median, coverage below peer norms, and a Significant indicative risk profile. Stable revenue growth and dependable cash generation offset thin margins, and distributions remain comfortably funded from free cash flow.

Our forward view is stable with limited upgrade potential near term; deleveraging toward the lower band would require sustained EBITDA growth or debt reduction rather than distributions. We would monitor margin pressure from input-cost volatility and any acceleration in shareholder returns that erodes the cash-flow cushion.

credit_strengths.text: 經營現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支與股東分派之總和，於派息及回購計劃後仍留有剩餘內部流動性。儘管批發雜貨利潤率微薄且絕對盈利能力有限，此自我融資能力仍支撐其投資級別狀況。
流動比率高於行業中位數並按年改善，反映有足夠營運資金支持日常餐飲服務分銷及短期限存貨周轉。流動性進一步由無限制現金結餘加強，按淨額基準實質抵銷總借貸。

key_risks.text: 風險因素指出行業以低利潤率為特徵，持續通脹或通縮影響產品成本及盈利能力。我們的經營利潤率遠低於行業中位數並按年轉弱，因此成本轉嫁時機仍是此分銷商的核心盈利敏感因素。
總槓桿高於行業中位數並按年略升，淨槓桿亦超過同業中位數。指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，與下一槓桿區間界限的緩衝空間狹窄，因此EBITDA輕微下降或新增借貸可能改變評估。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按絕對值而言足夠，但低於行業中位數並按年下降，以EBITDA為基礎的覆蓋率亦較同業疲弱。現金流對債務比率亦落後於行業中位數，顯示相對更依賴龐大債務結構而非內部產生現金。
到期結構可控，未來十二個月僅佔總借貸的一小部分，且並無任何單一年份出現集中的再融資牆。自由現金流對債務比率按年改善，支持我們判斷預定攤銷及到期款項可由內部資源應付。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們認為該信貸狀況穩健，但定位低於評級較高的分銷同業：槓桿高於行業中位數、覆蓋率低於同業常態，以及顯著的指示性風險狀況。穩定收入增長及可靠現金產生抵銷微薄利潤率，而分派仍由自由現金流輕鬆支持。
我們的前瞻觀點為穩定，短期內升級潛力有限；去槓桿至較低區間將需要持續EBITDA增長或債務減少，而非分派。我們將監察投入成本波動帶來的利潤率壓力，以及任何侵蝕現金流緩衝的股東回報加速。
